mainTopic: When and why we mention 'גבורות גשמים' in תפלה, the source for calling rain 'might', and the three keys God keeps for Himself
overview: The משנה asks from what day we start saying 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' in the עמידה. רבי אליעזר says from the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע says from שמיני עצרת, since rain on סוכות is a curse. רבי אליעזר answers that mentioning rain is praise, not a request, and רבי יהושע replies that then it could be said all year. The משנה adds that we ask for rain only close to the rainy season. רבי יהודה then says the mention begins at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and ends at מוסף of the first day of פסח. The גמרא first suggests the משנה builds on ברכות, but rejects that and says it follows ראש השנה's teaching that on סוכות the world is judged for water. It explains that rain is called 'גבורות' because a גזירה שוה on the word 'חקר' links rain to the creation of the world, which was done with גבורה. It learns from 'service of the heart' that rain belongs in תפלה. Finally, רבי יוחנן teaches that God keeps three keys for Himself, rain, birth and תחיית המתים, and the גמרא begins bringing a פסוק for each one, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opening question: from when do we mention rain?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks when we begin saying 'גבורות גשמים' in davening. רבי אליעזר says from the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע says from the last day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when do we mention the power of rain? רבי אליעזר says: from the first יום טוב of the חג (סוכות). רבי יהושע says: from the last יום טוב of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת by asking on what day we start adding the mention of rain in שמונה עשרה, and gives two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that rain is mentioned starting around סוכות. They disagree only about the exact day. רבי אליעזר starts on the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע waits until the last יום טוב, which is שמיני עצרת.

keyTerms.meaning: From when; from what point in time
We mention (praise, not a request)
The might of rain, which is God's power shown through rain
The Festival; in the משנה this means סוכות
The last festival day, which is שמיני עצרת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Mentioning' rain (מזכירין) is not the same as 'asking' for rain (שואלין). This משנה is about the praise line 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם', not the request 'ותן טל ומטר'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for when we begin saying 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' each year.

phrases.english: From when do we mention the might of the rains?
phrases.notes: This is the line 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' added in the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From the first Festival day of the Festival.
phrases.notes: In the משנה, 'the חג' with no other name always means סוכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From the last Festival day of the Festival.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute about when we start mentioning rain: רבי אליעזר says the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע says שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: rain on סוכות is a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר. Rain during סוכות is a bad sign, so why mention it then?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Since rain during the חג is only a sign of a curse, why should one mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's view. Why would we bring up rain during סוכות, when rain then is a bad thing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain during סוכות stops people from sitting in the סוכה, so it is a sign of a curse. Starting to mention rain on the first day of סוכות seems to invite something we don't want. This supports waiting until the חג is over.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because
A sign of a curse

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
Since the rains are nothing
other than a sign of a curse during the Festival,
why should he mention them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הוֹאִיל וְאֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים אֶלָּא סִימַן קְלָלָה בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's opinion from step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that we mention rain starting from the first day of סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain during סוכות is unwanted, a sign of a curse, so it makes no sense to mention it during the חג.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: mentioning is not asking
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he never said to ask for rain on סוכות. He only said to mention God's power of rain, which comes in its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I also did not say to ask for rain. I said only to mention 'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' in its season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends himself. He separates 'mentioning' rain as praise from 'asking' for rain as a request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's challenge only works if mentioning rain means wanting it now. רבי אליעזר says it does not. We are just praising God, who brings rain at the right time. So there is no problem saying it during סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask, which here means to request rain
To mention, as praise
In its season; at its proper time

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not agree that we should want rain on סוכות. He agrees it is a curse then. He just holds that mentioning rain is not a request for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
I too did not say to request
but only to mention
'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' in its season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי לִשְׁאוֹל אֶלָּא לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning rain on סוכות means asking for rain during the חג, which would be a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning rain is only praise of God's power, which brings rain in its proper time, so it is not a request for rain now.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: then mention it all year
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע replies: if mentioning is only praise, then we should mention rain all year round, even in summer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי יהושע) said to him: If so, one should always mention it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back against רבי אליעזר's answer. If mentioning is not a request, nothing would stop us from saying it every day of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we clearly do not mention rain all year, mentioning must have some link to the rainy season. So רבי אליעזר's distinction does not explain why he starts on the first day of סוכות. The משנה leaves this exchange here.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Always

steps.whatToRemember: The debate: רבי יהושע says rain on סוכות is a curse. רבי אליעזר says mentioning is not asking. רבי יהושע says then you should mention it all year.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע speaking again.

phrases.english: If so, one should always mention it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אִם כֵּן לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's answer from step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's distinction between mentioning and asking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If mentioning is pure praise with no link to wanting rain now, it should be said all year. Since it is not said all year, the distinction cannot explain starting on the first day of סוכות.

steps.title: We ask for rain only close to the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a general rule: the actual request for rain is made only close to the time rain is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not ask for rain except close to the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general rule about asking for rain, as opposed to mentioning it. The request is made only when the rainy season is near.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule fits with the discussion just before it. Asking for rain belongs near the time rain is actually needed and wanted. It also explains why you would not ask for rain early, during סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask, meaning we request rain
Close to; near

phrases.english: We do not request the rains
except close to the rains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שׁוֹאֲלִים אֶת הַגְּשָׁמִים אֶלָּא סָמוּךְ לַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule that builds on the mention/request distinction from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The request for rain is made only close to the rainy season.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: which שליח ציבור starts and stops
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the details. On שמיני עצרת, the later שליח ציבור (מוסף) starts mentioning rain. On the first day of פסח, the earlier one (שחרית) still mentions it, and the later one (מוסף) stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The one who leads the davening on the last יום טוב of סוכות: the last leader mentions rain and the first does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח: the first leader mentions rain and the last does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the exact point during the day when the mention of rain begins in the fall and ends in the spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שמיני עצרת, the change happens between שחרית and מוסף. The שחרית leader does not mention rain yet, and the מוסף leader starts. On the first day of פסח the reverse happens: שחרית still mentions rain, and מוסף stops. So the season begins and ends at the same point in the day.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark, meaning the שליח ציבור
The first leader (שחרית)
The last leader (מוסף)
Passover, when the mention of rain ends

steps.whatToRemember: The mention of rain starts at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and ends at מוסף of the first day of פסח. This is how we practice today.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the שליח ציבור announces 'משיב הרוח' before מוסף on שמיני עצרת, and why we stop at מוסף of the first day of פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The one who passes before the ark
phrases.notes: This means the person leading the davening, the שליח ציבור.

phrases.english: on the last Festival day of the Festival —
the last one mentions, the first one does not mention.
phrases.notes: The 'first' one leads שחרית and the 'last' one leads מוסף.

phrases.english: On the first Festival day of Passover —
the first one mentions, the last one does not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds practical details about the exact start and end of the mention of rain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mention of rain begins at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and ends at מוסף of the first day of פסח.

steps.title: Where is the משנה coming from when it asks 'from when'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what earlier source the תנא is relying on. Asking 'from when' assumes we already know there is a duty to mention rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Where is the תנא standing, that he teaches 'from when'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the משנה's first word. Asking 'from when' assumes the duty to mention rain was already taught somewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question like 'from when do we mention' only makes sense if we already know that we mention rain at all. The גמרא wants to know where that basic duty was taught. It is not asking about the date here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The author of the משנה
Where is he standing, meaning what source is he building on?
That he teaches

phrases.english: GEMARA: Where is the tanna standing,
phrases.notes: In other words, what earlier teaching is the תנא leaning on?

phrases.english: that he teaches 'From when'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the opening word of the משנה from step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What earlier source establishes the basic duty to mention rain, which the משנה's 'from when' assumes?

steps.title: The תנא is relying on a source 'there'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the תנא is building on a teaching found in another place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is standing there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by pointing to an earlier source elsewhere. It names that source in the next lines, so this answer is still being set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the duty to mention rain was already taught in a different משנה. Our משנה picks up from there and only asks when it starts. The specific source is spelled out right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in another place

phrases.english: The tanna is standing there —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא is building on an earlier teaching found elsewhere, which already established the duty to mention rain. The source is identified in the continuation.

steps.title: The earlier source is the משנה in ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the source the תנא relies on: the משנה in ברכות that places rain-mentioning in תחיית המתים, rain-asking in ברכת השנים, and הבדלה in חונן הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה there teaches: we mention the might of rain in the blessing of תחיית המתים, we ask for rain in ברכת השנים, and we say הבדלה in חונן הדעת. And based on that, our משנה teaches: from when do we mention the might of rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 8 by quoting the earlier משנה that already tells us we must mention rain. Our משנה just adds the 'when'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא noticed that asking 'from when' assumes we already know about a duty to mention rain. Here it shows where that duty comes from: the משנה in ברכות, which tells us where in the עמידה rain is mentioned. Our משנה builds on that by telling us the time of year.

keyTerms.meaning: Resurrection of the dead; the second blessing of the עמידה, where 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' is said
The blessing of the years; the ninth blessing of the עמידה, where we ask for rain
Separating holy time from regular time, said on מוצאי שבת and יום טוב
'Who grants knowledge'; the fourth blessing of the עמידה
Mentioning (praising God for rain) versus asking (requesting rain)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'mentioning' rain with 'asking' for rain. They are two different things said in two different blessings.

phrases.english: As it teaches: we mention the might of rain
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מסכת ברכות 33a.

phrases.english: in the blessing of the resurrection of the dead,
and we ask for rain in the blessing of the years,
and הבדלה is said in 'Who grants knowledge.'
And so it teaches here: from when do we mention the might of rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 8 by quoting the actual source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The underlying source is the משנה in ברכות that obligates mentioning rain in תחיית המתים.

steps.title: Then why not teach it in ברכות?
steps.stepSummary: If this law continues the משנה in ברכות, it should have been taught there. Why wait until מסכת תענית?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the תנא teach it there! What is different, that he left it all the way until here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If our משנה is a follow-up to ברכות, why is it not in ברכות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a follow-up law is taught right next to the law it builds on. ברכות is at the start of סדר זרעים, and תענית is deep in סדר מועד. So the gap needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So let him teach it there!' A challenge about where something should be taught
What is different?
He left it / put it aside

phrases.english: But let him teach it there!
phrases.notes: 'There' means in מסכת ברכות, right after the rule about where rain is mentioned.

phrases.english: What is different, that he left it until here?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the placement implied by step 9's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה builds on the משנה in ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is a continuation of ברכות, it belongs in ברכות, not far away in תענית.

steps.title: The תנא is coming straight from ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא just finished ראש השנה, which said that on חג the world is judged for water. That led him to teach about mentioning rain right here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא is coming from ראש השנה, as we learned there: 'On חג (סוכות) the world is judged for water.' And since he taught that, he went on to teach: from when do we mention the might of rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining why this law appears here and not in ברכות. The trigger is the משנה in ראש השנה about the judgment for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'אלא' the גמרא drops its first answer, that the תנא is standing on ברכות. Instead it says the תנא is building on the משנה in ראש השנה. Since the world is judged for water on סוכות, it is natural to teach next when we start mentioning rain, which also happens at סוכות time.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'went up / finished'; the תנא just came from finishing that מסכת
Are judged for water: how much rain the world will get
'The Festival', here meaning סוכות
Since / because he was already dealing with

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the order of the משניות can follow a flow of topics, not only the source of the law.

phrases.english: Rather, the tanna came here from Rosh HaShana,
phrases.notes: He means the תנא had just finished teaching מסכת ראש השנה.

phrases.english: as we learned: and on the Festival they are judged for water.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא וּבֶחָג נִידּוֹנִים עַל הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: And since he taught 'and on the Festival they are judged for water,'
he taught: from when do we mention the might of rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the placement through the order of the מסכתות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the law builds on ברכות, it should have been taught there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא is coming here from מסכת ראש השנה, which taught that on סוכות the world is judged for water. That naturally leads to asking when we start mentioning rain.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's final answer is that the תנא of תענית is building on ראש השנה, not ברכות. ראש השנה taught that on סוכות the world is judged for water, and that leads into 'from when do we mention the might of rain.'

steps.title: Why say 'the might of rain'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the wording: why not just say 'mention rain' instead of 'mention the might of rain'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה simply say: 'From when do we mention rain.' What is meant by 'the might of rain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a new question about the wording of the משנה. It wants to know why the extra word 'might' is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shorter phrase would have been enough to teach the law. So the extra word 'גבורות' must be telling us something about how we see rain.

keyTerms.meaning: The might (powerful acts) of rain
What is? What does it mean?

phrases.english: And let him teach: 'From when do we mention rain.'
What is 'the might of rain'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה adds the word 'גבורות' (might) when describing rain.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: rain falls with God's might
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that rain falls with power, and brings פסוקים from איוב that list rain among God's great wonders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because rain falls with might. As it says: 'Who does great things beyond understanding, wonders without number.' And it is written: 'Who gives rain upon the earth, and sends water upon the fields.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the wording question: rain is called 'might' because it shows God's power. He proves it from two side-by-side פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק speaks of God's great, uncountable wonders. The very next פסוק talks about rain. That shows rain is one of those mighty wonders, so the משנה calls it 'גבורות גשמים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Might, power
Searching out, full understanding
And it is written: brings a second פסוק
Open places, fields

steps.whatToRemember: We say 'גבורות גשמים' because rain is one of God's mighty wonders, as the פסוקים in איוב show.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because they fall with might,
as it is said: 'Who does great things beyond understanding,
phrases.notes: איוב 5:9

phrases.english: and wonders without number,'
and it is written: 'Who gives rain upon the earth,
phrases.notes: איוב 5:10, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: and sends water upon the fields.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיּוֹרְדִין בִּגְבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain is called 'גבורות' because it falls with Divine might, shown by the פסוקים in איוב that place rain among God's great wonders.

steps.title: How do these פסוקים show that rain is might?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוקים in איוב show that rain is a display of God's גבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. The פסוקים call rain a great wonder, but they never use the word 'might', so the גמרא asks where that idea comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that rain is a great, mysterious act. But the משנה's word is גבורה (might). The גמרא wants a link that ties rain to גבורה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is this implied? How do we see it?

phrases.english: From where is it implied?
phrases.notes: He means: where do those פסוקים in איוב show that rain is an act of might?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the missing link in רבי יוחנן's proof from איוב
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוקים in איוב prove that rain specifically shows גבורה

steps.title: A word link to the creation of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא answers with a גזירה שוה: the word 'חקר' appears both with rain and with בריאת העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: We learn it from the word 'comprehension' here and 'comprehension' in the passage about the creation of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא gives the method of the answer. A shared word links rain to the creation of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה connects two places in תנ״ך that use the same word, so what is true in one applies to the other. Here the shared word is 'חקר' (beyond understanding). The details come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from; we learn it from (a word link)
Searching out, comprehension
The creation of the world

steps.title: The פסוקים that complete the word link
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא lays out the פסוקים: rain is 'beyond comprehension', creation is 'beyond comprehension', and creation is done 'with might'. So rain is also might.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here: 'He does great things beyond comprehension.' And it says there: 'Have you not known, have you not heard, that the everlasting God, ה׳, Creator of the ends of the earth, does not grow faint or weary? His understanding is beyond comprehension.' And it says: 'He sets up the mountains with His strength, girded with might.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא lays out the three פסוקים behind his word link. Together they show that rain, like creation, is an act of גבורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Link 1: the פסוק about rain says 'אין חקר'. Link 2: the פסוק about creation also says 'אין חקר', so rain and creation are connected. Link 3: another פסוק says creation was done 'בגבורה', so rain is also גבורה.

steps.title: Why mention rain in תפלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that rain belongs in תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that it belongs in prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. We know why rain is called גבורה, but why should it be mentioned in תפלה at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining the name 'גבורות גשמים' does not explain why it belongs in the עמידה. The גמרא now asks for a source for that.

steps.title: Service of the heart, then rain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'serving God with all your heart' means תפלה. The very next פסוק talks about rain, so rain belongs in תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'To love ה׳ your God and to serve Him with all your heart.' What service is done in the heart? You must say it is prayer. And right after it is written: 'I will give the rain of your land in its time, the early rain and the late rain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer. 'Service of the heart' is תפלה, and the next פסוק promises rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the ברייתא shows that 'עבודה שבלב' means תפלה. Then the גמרא points out that rain is mentioned right after it. Because the two sit side by side, rain is connected to תפלה.

steps.title: Three keys God keeps for Himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that God personally holds three keys and never handed them to a messenger: rain, birth, and תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and were never given to a messenger. They are: the key of rain, the key of birth, and the key of the resurrection of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן. It lists three things God does Himself, with rain first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new idea: rain is so special that God handles it directly, with no שליח. Rain and תחיית המתים are on the same list, which fits why rain is mentioned in the ברכה of תחיית המתים (step 9).

steps.title: The פסוק for the key of rain
steps.stepSummary: The key of rain is proven from a פסוק in דברים: 'ה׳ will open for you His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The key of rain is in God's hands, as the פסוק says: 'ה׳ will open for you His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first of רבי יוחנן's three keys, rain, with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ Himself will 'open' the heavens to give rain. 'Opening' is what a key does, and the פסוק names ה׳ as the one who opens, with no messenger. That supports רבי יוחנן's claim that the key of rain never leaves God's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Key, the thing that opens something locked

steps.title: The פסוק for the key of birth begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the key of birth and starts quoting the פסוק about God remembering רחל. The פסוק continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn the key of birth? As it is written: 'And אלהים remembered רחל, and listened…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second key, birth, asks for its source, and begins quoting the פסוק. The quote is cut off here and finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model is the same as for rain. רחל could not have children until God Himself remembered her. The key word, 'opened' (her womb), comes later in the פסוק, so the full proof is completed in the next section.
